events.body: Rider alleges dangerous driving (speeding, hard braking, shoulder overtaking) on trip Jurong East MRT → NUS, 21:22–21:34, fare $21.04 fixed; SAFE-2 requires a human reviewer. Record contains no measurement of speed, braking or shoulder use: GPS shows only distance and time [F1][F2]; the complete, fully timestamped 2-message chat is pickup logistics only [F3][F4][F5]; the driver's post-trip statement denies any complaint was made [F6]; both profiles show 0 disputes / 0 upheld in 90 d [F7][F8]. Disputed: the manner of driving, which only the rider's complaint and the driver's denial speak to.

events.title: Notices sent to rider and driver
events.body:
RIDER: Your safety report about the Jurong East MRT to NUS RydeX trip has been sent to a human safety reviewer. The reviewer will look at your account of the driver speeding, braking hard and overtaking on the shoulder, and at the trip details on file. Nothing has been decided yet. Your fare is unchanged — the $21.04 RydeX quote stands, so no refund or voucher applies here. If you were in danger, you can call 995; you can also report the driving directly to the driver's commercial motor insurer, or through RydeHELP in the app. Your account is unaffected.

DRIVER: A rider safety report about your Jurong East MRT to NUS RydeX trip has been sent to a human safety reviewer. The reviewer will look at the rider's account of speeding, hard braking throughout and overtaking on the shoulder, along with the trip details on file. Nothing has been decided yet. Your fare is unchanged — the $21.04 RydeX quote stands, so no payment or voucher is being issued either way. Your account stays active and is not being flagged. If the reviewer needs anything from you, you will be contacted separately.

ruling.recommended_action: Route the file to a human safety reviewer with the summary below; note the 995 / driver's commercial motor insurance / RydeHELP reporting paths to the rider; take no fare action ($21.04 fixed RydeX quote stands); do not flag either account.
ruling.reasoning: This is a rider-filed safety case: the complaint alleges the driver was speeding, braking hard throughout, and overtaking on the shoulder on the RydeX trip Jurong East MRT → NUS (pickup 21:22, drop-off 21:34), and that the rider was scared. That is a dangerous-driving allegation, and under SAFE-2 such a case is not decided automatically but sent to a human reviewer, with the 995 / driver's commercial motor insurance / RydeHELP reporting paths noted [SAFE-2]. The policy execution trace marks the SAFE-1 screening as passed with escalate as the only permitted outcome, so no monetary ruling is available on this file.

rejected_claims.reason: Not rejected as to outcome — escalation is granted under SAFE-2 on the rider's dangerous-driving allegation. Recorded only to note that the rider's own brief offers no independent evidence of the manoeuvres beyond the complaint narrative; SAFE-2 does not require corroboration for escalation, so this does not change the outcome [F5][F6][SAFE-2].

Not rejected — but the assertion that escalation 'rests on ... the absence of any record refuting it' is not adopted: missing evidence is never treated as favouring either side. Escalation rests on the dangerous-driving allegation itself, which SAFE-2 requires a human to review [F1][F5][SAFE-2].
Not rejected — the driver's post-trip statement cannot waive or displace a safety report under SAFE-1/SAFE-2; it is recorded as the driver's account and nothing more [F6][SAFE-1][SAFE-2].

Not rejected — with no off-route segment [F1] and no traffic fact, there is no routing violation and no routing excuse in this file, but RD-1/RD-4 govern route deviation, not the manner of driving, so they neither establish nor dispose of the safety complaint [F1][F2][RD-1][RD-4].
Not rejected — no fare defect is alleged or evidenced: the fare is a fixed RydeX quote and no unpublished add-on appears, so no amount is computable and only escalation is sought [F1][F2][FARE-1].
Not rejected — F7/F8 are correctly treated as context only; profile facts cannot decide a case on their own, and no flag_account is sought or granted [F7][F8][RD-6].

Not rejected — the driver does not contest escalation, but his request that the summary 'record his clean record' cannot convert the file into a finding of no unsafe driving; the escalation stands on the allegation, and the summary carries both accounts [F6][F8][SAFE-2].

Rejected as a ground for resolution — the GPS record shows only 8.5 km vs 8.6 km optimal [F1] and 12.8 min vs a 14 min estimate [F2]; these measure distance and elapsed time, not speed profile, braking or lane use, so they neither corroborate nor disprove the dangerous-driving allegation, and SAFE-2 escalation is not defeated by a neutral distance/duration record [F1][F2][SAFE-2].

Rejected as a ground for resolution — the complete timestamped chat contains only pickup logistics [F3][F4][F5], which shows silence in the in-app channel, not that the alleged driving was safe or that the rider consented to it; a rider's not complaining in chat is not evidence of anything beyond silence, and the post-trip statement in [F6] is self-serving [F3][F4][F5][F6][SAFE-1][SAFE-2].

Not rejected — the rider makes no threat/intimidation/harassment allegation against the driver and the chat holds none, so SAFE-1 is not triggered on that ground; escalation here rests on SAFE-2 dangerous driving, not on SAFE-1 [F3][F4][F5][F6][SAFE-1]

Not rejected — no flag_account is sought by either side and the driver's history (3.5 y, 4.82 rating, 345 trips, 0 disputes / 0 upheld in 90 d) gives no basis; profile facts can never decide the case and the flag action is therefore not applied [F8][RD-6]

Not rejected — the $21.04 was the fixed RydeX quote and no surcharge, excess distance or unpublished add-on appears, so there is nothing to refund; but this does not dispose of the safety complaint, which is escalated under SAFE-2 [F1][FARE-1][SAFE-2]

ruling.evidence_gap: No fact in the file measures speed, braking behaviour or shoulder use, and there is no traffic/road record or any third-party observation for this trip. The rider's complaint narrative is the only account of the driving; the driver's statement [F6] is a post-trip denial. A reviewer would need the rider's detailed account (times/locations of the alleged manoeuvres) and any available vehicle telematics or camera footage to settle whether any of the alleged manoeuvres occurred.

actions.detail: Rider alleges dangerous driving (speeding, hard braking, shoulder overtaking) on trip Jurong East MRT → NUS, 21:22–21:34, fare $21.04 fixed; SAFE-2 requires a human reviewer. Record contains no measurement of speed, braking or shoulder use: GPS shows only distance and time [F1][F2]; the complete, fully timestamped 2-message chat is pickup logistics only [F3][F4][F5]; the driver's post-trip statement denies any complaint was made [F6]; both profiles show 0 disputes / 0 upheld in 90 d [F7][F8]. Disputed: the manner of driving, which only the rider's complaint and the driver's denial speak to.

claims.assertion: The rider's complaint states the driver was speeding, braking hard and overtaking on the shoulder, and that she was scared and felt unsafe — this is a dangerous-driving allegation, so the case must be sent to a human reviewer under SAFE-2 with the 995 / driver's commercial motor insurance / RydeHELP reporting paths noted, not decided automatically.

The rider's safety allegation is not contradicted by any system record in this file: the GPS record shows a negative deviation with actual 8.5 km vs optimal 8.6 km (F1) and the chat log is complete (F5), so the escalation rests on the rider's own contemporaneous account plus the absence of any record refuting it.

The driver's post-trip written statement (F6) asserts 'I drove normally' and that the rider never complained; a statement written after the trip cannot displace the rider's complaint about driving conduct, and it carries no weight as consent or as a waiver of a safety report.

No exemption or excuse based on route can be relied on to explain the conduct: there is no off-route segment in the facts (F1) and no traffic or weather record of any kind for this trip, so nothing in the case file supports a claim that the manoeuvres were forced by congestion, an incident or road closure.

The fare is a fixed RydeX quote and no fare defect is alleged or evidenced, so the rider does not seek a fare refund and requests only that the safety complaint be escalated; the requested outcome is limited to escalate, with no monetary amount computable from the facts.

The driver's account is long-standing but has no violation history (F8) and the rider has 0 disputes in 90 days (F7); those profile facts are offered only as context and cannot decide this safety dispute either way.

weaknesses: The only evidence of the driving conduct is the rider's own narrative quoted in the complaint; the chat record itself (F3, F4, F5) contains nothing about speeding, hard braking or shoulder overtaking, so the driver will argue the rider never raised it at the time.

The system records are neutral to favourable to the driver on route and timing: F1 shows actual distance 8.5 km vs optimal 8.6 km and F2 shows the trip finished 1.0 min faster than the 14 min estimate, which the driver will use to argue the ride was normal.

The driver's statement (F6) says the rider was on the phone throughout and never complained, which the driver will use against the rider's credibility; I rely on the fact that a post-trip written statement cannot override a safety report, but it is still an honest weak point.
No traffic/weather facts exist for this trip, so I cannot point to any external record that a third party observed the alleged driving.
Profile facts (F7, F8) show 0 prior disputes and 0 upheld for the driver, which weakens any suggestion of a pattern; I therefore do not request flag_account.

claims.assertion: The complaint is a dangerous-driving allegation ('speeding and braking hard the whole way, overtaking on the shoulder'), which under SAFE-2 must go to a human reviewer rather than be resolved as an automated fare/route ruling; the driver does not contest escalation and asks that the escalated summary record his clean record.

The objective GPS record contradicts the manner-of-driving allegations in the only measurable respect available: the trip took 12.8 min against a 14 min estimate (F2) over 8.5 km versus an 8.6 km optimal route (F1), i.e. the driver neither detoured nor gained time, so there is no system evidence of the excessive speed the rider describes.

The rider never raised any safety concern during or after the trip in the in-app channel: the complete, fully timestamped 2-message record contains only pickup logistics (F3, F4, F5), and the driver's contemporaneous statement records that the rider stayed on the phone and never complained (F6).
There is no threat, intimidation or harassment by the driver anywhere in the chat record (F3, F4, F5), so SAFE-1's escalation ground is not triggered by anything the driver said or wrote.

No corroborating profile pattern supports a flag against this driver: 3.5 years on the platform, 4.82 rating, 345 trips in 90 days and 0 disputes / 0 upheld in 90 days (F8); a flag_account request is not justified on this record.
The $21.04 was the fixed RydeX quote and no fare fact shows any surcharge, excess distance or unpublished add-on, so there is nothing to refund even if the rider's description were accepted.

weaknesses: The rider's own complaint (as indexed) is the only account of the manner of driving, and no fact in the table measures speed, braking or shoulder use — GPS facts F1 and F2 speak only to distance and elapsed time, so they cannot affirmatively disprove speeding on a short 8.5 km trip.

The rider had a 4.5 rating with 0 disputes in 90 days (F7), a plausible non-chronic complainant, which makes the 'never complained' point in F6 weaker; the driver's statement F6 that the rider 'never complained' is itself a self-serving statement the other side will say is contradicted by the filing of this dispute.

My D4 argument only addresses driver-side threatening language; SAFE-1/Safe-2 escalation is mandatory regardless of how clean the chat is, so the realistic outcome remains escalate, not no_action, and the rider's safety allegation stays live for the human reviewer.
The chat record F5 is complete and timestamped, so I cannot argue for a G12 'evidence incomplete' route to undetermined; the record's silence is the only thing I have.

points.response: Agreed that SAFE-2 sends this to a human, and the rider raises no objection to the driver's clean record (F8) being included in that summary — but escalation is the floor, not a finding of 'no unsafe driving', so the driver gains nothing he can enforce from agreeing to it.

No detour and no time gained (F1, F2) is exactly what one expects on a short 8.5 km urban trip and says nothing about speed, braking or shoulder use; SAFE-2 is triggered by the dangerous-driving allegation itself, so a neutral distance/duration record (F1, F2) cannot resolve the safety question either way.

The chat log (F3, F4) contains only pickup logistics because the rider was a passenger in a moving car, not a correspondent, and F5 confirms the record is complete and merely silent; the driver's post-trip statement F6 that she 'never complained' is self-serving and is directly contradicted by this filed safety dispute (F7 shows a 4.5-rated rider with 0 disputes), and a rider's silence in-app is not consent to dangerous driving.

Conceded — the rider makes no threat/intimidation/harassment allegation against the driver and relies on SAFE-2 (dangerous driving), not SAFE-1; escalation here is mandatory on the dangerous-driving ground regardless of the chat's content.

The rider does not ask for a flag_account and expressly withdraws any profile-based suggestion; F8 (3.5 y, 4.82, 345 trips, 0 upheld) is context only and, per RD-6's own terms, profile facts can never decide a case, so no flag is sought on either side.

Conceded — the rider seeks no money: $21.04 was the fixed RydeX quote and no surcharge, excess distance or unpublished add-on appears in the facts, so the sole relief sought is the escalation required by SAFE-2.

I do not contest escalation on the safety allegation; my client's position is that the escalated summary must be accurate, and the only measurable system evidence in the file is that the trip was 8.5 km against an 8.6 km optimal route (F1) and finished in 12.8 min against a 14 min estimate (F2).

I agree no record in the file measures speed or braking; the negative deviation in F1 and the faster-than-estimate time in F2 are equally consistent with ordinary driving, so they cannot be read as corroboration of the rider's account either.

I accept a post-trip statement (F6) cannot waive a safety report, but the rider's silence cuts against her account on credibility: the complete, fully timestamped chat record (F3, F4, F5) contains only pickup logistics, and nothing in it reports speeding, hard braking or shoulder overtaking at the time.

The absence of any off-route segment (F1) and of any traffic record is not evidence of dangerous driving; RD-1 and RD-4 govern whether a route deviation was justified, and with no off-route segment (F1) there is no routing violation to attach to my client.

I agree no refund is sought or owing — the RydeX fare was the fixed quote and no fare fact shows any unpublished add-on — so the driver's exposure in this case is limited to the safety escalation, not to money.

The rider is right that profile facts cannot decide the case, and they give no basis to flag the driver: 3.5 years on the platform, 4.82 rating, 345 trips in 90 days with 0 disputes and 0 upheld (F8), against the rider's 0 disputes in 90 days (F7).

I maintain D5: profile facts may support a flag_account request but never the main finding (RD-6), and here the driver's history of 0 disputes and 0 upheld in 90 days (F8) affirmatively weighs against any account action on this file.
